content:
Apple CEO Tim Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week to meet King Charles, as part of a new partnership between Apple and The King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down for an in-depth interview with The Independent to discuss the partnership and his first month as Apple's executive chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, handing the reins to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook said the transition 'actually began several years ago.'

Ternus took over as CEO just as the iPhone Duo was launching, and Cook said the product was already completely mapped out. Cook explained: 'I wanted John's first day to go smoothly, and a lot of Apple's tailwind comes from the product cycle.'

Cook also stressed that as Apple's executive chairman, he is focused on 'global policy' matters, and mentioned that he and Ternus have 'a very high level of trust.' Cook will assist Ternus in whatever way he sees fit, but made clear that he will 'not interfere.'

What advice did Cook give Ternus? 'Don't try to be me.' To read the full interview, head to The Independent's website, which also covers the latest Apple and King's Trust partnership in detail.
